title: Robust differentiation of human embryonic stem cells into definitive endoderm using Activin A coupled with mTOR inhibition.
protocol: Reconstitute 10 µg of Activin in 200 µl DPBS supplemented with 0.2% (w/v) BSA.
Store the Activin solution at -20°C in 10 µl aliquots for up to 6 months.
Defrost Activin aliquots at 4°C and use within 3 days after thawing.
Reconstitute 1 mg of FGF-2 in 100 ml DPBS supplemented with 0.2% (w/v) BSA.
Filter the FGF-2 solution using a 0.22 µm filter unit.
Store the filtered FGF-2 at -20°C in 1 ml aliquots for up to 12 months.
Defrost FGF-2 aliquots at 4°C and use within 1 month after thawing.
Reconstitute 2 µg of BMP2 in 100 µl DPBS supplemented with 0.2% (w/v) BSA.
Store the BMP2 solution at -20°C in 10 µl aliquots for up to 6 months.
Defrost BMP2 aliquots at 4°C and use within 3 days after thawing.
Dissolve 100 mg of Insulin in 10 ml sterile 0.01 M HCl solution supplemented with 0.2% (w/v) BSA overnight at 4°C.
Store the Insulin solution at -20°C in 10 µl aliquots for up to 6 months.
Defrost Insulin aliquots at 4°C and use within 3 days after thawing.
Dissolve 1 g of Hydrocortisone-21-hemisuccinate in 20 ml cell culture grade water.
Store the Hydrocortisone solution at -20°C in 1 ml aliquots for up to 12 months.
Defrost Hydrocortisone aliquots at 4°C and use within 2 weeks after thawing.
Dissolve 0.5 g of Ascorbic acid in 10 ml cell culture grade water.
Store the Ascorbic acid solution at -20°C in 1 ml aliquots for up to 12 months.
Defrost Ascorbic acid aliquots at 4°C and use within 2 weeks after thawing.
Reconstitute ascorbic acid in the dark or wrapped in aluminium foil.
Mix 10 μg HGF with 1 ml DPBS supplemented with 0.2% (w/v) BSA.
Store defrosted HGF aliquots at 4°C and use within 2 weeks.
Mix 10 μg OSM with 1 ml DPBS supplemented with 0.2% (w/v) BSA.
Store defrosted OSM aliquots at 4°C and use within 2 weeks.
Dissolve 10 mg Torin-2 in 2.3 ml DMSO Hybri-MaxTM.
Aliquot Torin-2 solution into 100 μl portions and store at -20°C for up to 12 months.
Store defrosted Torin-2 aliquots at 4°C and use within 1 month.
Handle Torin-2 with care due to DMSO penetration risk.
In a cell culture hood, mix 400 ml KO-DMEM with 100 ml KSR (20%).
Add 2.5 ml M L-glutamine (1 mM), 5 ml non-essential amino acids (1X), and 1 ml β-mercaptoethanol (0.1 M) to the mixture.
Filter the KO-DMEM-KSR medium using a PES vacuum filter (0.22 μm).
Store filtered KSR medium at 4°C for up to 1 week.
Aliquot unused KSR upon first use and store at -80°C.
Add ROCK inhibitor and FGF-2 to MEF-CM to achieve final concentrations of 10 µM and 10 ng/ml, respectively.
Dissolve 36.4 mg of collagenase powder in 50 ml of KO-DMEM.
Filter sterilize the collagenase solution using a 0.22 µm filter unit.
Aliquot and store the filtered collagenase solution at -20°C.
Thaw the aliquot of collagenase just before use at 37°C.
Under sterile conditions, add 1 ml of B27 supplement to 50 ml of RPMI AQmedia.
Filter sterilize the mixture using a 0.22 µm filter unit.
Store the DE induction medium at 4°C for up to one week.
Add Activin and Torin to achieve final concentrations of 100 ng/ml and 15 nM, respectively, before use.
Under sterile conditions, add BMP-2 and FGF-2 to KSR medium to achieve final concentrations of 20 ng/ml and 10 ng/ml, respectively.
Base hepatoblast specification medium can be stored at 4°C for up to two weeks.
Prepare 500 ml of L-15 medium supplemented with 8.4% tryptose phosphate broth, 8.3% FBS, 2 mM L-Glutamine, 10 µM hydrocortisone-21-hemisuccinate, and 1 µM insulin.
Store the hepatocyte maturation base medium at 4°C for up to two weeks.
Supplement with 50 µg/ml ascorbic acid, 20 ng/ml OSM, and 10 ng/ml HGF immediately before use.
Thaw stock Matrigel overnight on ice at 4 °C.
Dilute thawed Matrigel 1 in 2 with chilled KO-DMEM.
Aliquot diluted Matrigel into 15 ml tubes at 1 ml per tube and store at -20 °C.
Thaw an aliquot of stored Matrigel at 4 °C overnight before use.
Dilute thawed aliquot 1 in 15 with chilled KO-DMEM for coating plates.
Coat each well of one 6-well plate with 1 ml of the diluted Matrigel solution.
Allow coated plates to set at 4 °C overnight.
Warm coated plates at room temperature for at least 20 min before use.
Seal plates with parafilm to prevent evaporation and store at 4 °C until needed.
Aspirate excess Matrigel solution from the wells upon use.
Replace aspirated Matrigel with MEF-CM prior to hESC passaging.
Thaw frozen MEFs (passage 0) and grow in DMEM AQmedia containing 10% FBS.
Passage the cells 3 to 4 times to obtain sufficient number of vigorously growing cells.
Trypsinise the cells and irradiate for 40 Gy using a cell irradiator to abolish their replicative potential.
Seed irradiated MEFs at a density of 2.5 x 10^7 cells into T225 flasks pre-coated with 0.5% gelatin for 20 min.
Allow the cells to plate down overnight.
Rinse cells once with DPBS the following day.
Replace growth medium with 150 ml KSR medium supplemented with 4 ng/ml FGF-2.
Collect MEF-CM after allowing MEFs to condition the media for 24 hours.
Freeze collected MEF-CM at -80 °C immediately.
Repeat collection of MEF-CM for up to 7 days.
Thaw bottles of frozen MEF-CM in a water bath until fully defrosted.
Supplement thawed MEF-CM with 1 mM L-Glutamine.
Filter the supplemented medium through a 0.22 μm filter unit to remove residual MEF cell debris.
Take out required volume for daily feed and warm it up.
Store leftover medium at 4 °C for up to a week.
Supplement medium with 10 ng/ml FGF-2 immediately prior to addition to hESCs.
Culture hESCs as colonies with daily exchange of complete MEF-CM for 5-7 days.
Ensure a warmed Matrigel plate contains 2 ml per well MEF-CM before passaging.
Treat one well of hESCs with 1 ml collagenase IV for 5 to 10 min.
Rinse treated wells with DPBS.
Replace DPBS with 1 ml MEF-CM and gently scrape colonies using the tip of a 5 ml pipette.
Add an additional 2 ml MEF-CM and break up colonies by gentle pipetting 3-4 times.
Transfer 1 ml of cell solution into 3 wells of a new plate to achieve a 1:3 split.
Defrost and warm Accutase solution and KO-DMEM to 37 °C.
Warm an appropriate Matrigel gel plate to room temperature.
Aspirate off MEF-CM and rinse cells once with DPBS.
Exchange DPBS with 1 ml warm Accutase solution for one well.
Incubate with Accutase for 5 to 10 min until colonies disassociate into single cells.
Neutralize Accutase solution with 2 ml of KO-DMEM per well.
Pipette cell suspension through a 1 ml Gilson pipette tip to dissociate clumps further.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 ml tube and centrifuge at 60g for 5 min.
Prepare Matrigel plates by transferring 2 ml MEF-CM containing FGF-2 and ROCK inhibitor into each well.
Aspirate supernatant after centrifugation and resuspend cell pellet in 3 ml MEF-CM supplemented with FGF-2 and ROCK inhibitor.
Dispense 1 ml per well of the new plate to achieve a 1:3 split.
Allow cells to plate down overnight and verify formation of a homogenous cell monolayer the following day.
Exchange medium with fresh MEF-CM containing only FGF-2 and incubate overnight.
Warm an appropriate aliquot of DE induction medium to 37 °C.
Supplement DE induction medium with Activin at 100 ng ml-1 and Torin at 15 nM.
Exchange the medium with MEF-CM to induce DE differentiation.
Observe cells daily for key phenotypic changes reflecting progress in differentiation.
The following day, cells will start to adopt a spiky morphology reminiscent of primitive streak cells and appear as spiked clusters.
Exchange medium from Step 10 for another day to continue differentiation.
By day 2 of differentiation, the majority of cells will adopt a spiky morphology; clusters will begin to disperse due to EMT-induced cell mobility.
Again, exchange medium to complete DE differentiation.
By day 3, differentiation should largely be complete; clusters should be minimal or absent and predominantly polygonal-shaped cells should appear.
Initiate hepatoblast specification by exchanging DE induction medium with hepatoblast specification medium supplemented with 20 ng ml^-1 BMP-2 and 10 ng ml^-1 FGF-2.
Split cultures onto Matrigel-coated plates using Accutase at a 1:2 ratio if cells become too confluent due to low Torin cytotoxicity.
Exchange media daily and observe phenotypic changes to track differentiation progress.
Cells initially increase in size but maintain a rough border between each other.
Border becomes more pronounced as differentiation proceeds.
After 3-5 days, cells largely adopt polygonal morphology characteristic of hepatoblasts.
More mature features such as prominent nucleus and binucleated cells remain absent.
Exchange the hepatoblast specification medium with hepatocyte maturation medium supplemented with OSM (20 ng/ml), HGF (10 ng/ml), and ascorbic acid (50 µg/ml).
Cells visibly increase in size during hepatocyte maturation.
Cell-cell borders become more reinforced and prominent.
Mononucleated and binucleated cells appear with increasing frequency.
By latter stages, cells begin to accumulate lipid droplets.
At this stage, cells can be taken for functional assays or lysed for gene expression or protein analysis.
Cells can be kept in this state for no longer than 3 days.
